procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires factory registration before a certificate of origin can be applied for; registration needs the factory to be outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added, and takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade provides the e-service: log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the Certificate of Origin for India service, fill in the application form, upload proof of factory registration and the commercial invoice (plus the factory's purchase invoice if a trading exporter), pay the fee online and submit; processing takes about one working day.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for an invoice value up to AED 100000.

The competent authority issues the certificate: it is valid for 12 months from issue, covers one import, and should be issued before, at or within 5 working days of export; it can be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 of India's form.

The exporter ships the goods directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading or storage. If a third party issues the invoice, the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information including which criterion is claimed, keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing and answers customs requests within 10 working days.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

caveats.note: The '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 45%' is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
The final manufacture and the operations described are the exporter's own declaration.
India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ from the estimate shown.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only; IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022), not the official text.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India.
The 40% value-added letter is a Factory Registration condition only; it is NOT the CEPA product-specific rule test, which is set per tariff line.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
De minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).
